docs.purpose: Where a visitor signs in or creates an account. It offers email-and-password sign-in, a sign-up form that also collects a name and whether the account is an individual or a company, and a Google sign-in button. Administrators with two-factor turned on get a second box asking for the six-digit code from their authenticator app. When the visitor was bounced here from a page that needed a login, it sends them back to that page afterwards, and only to pages on this site.
docs.data_story: This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the GATE renderer (a `statuses_handled[]` that must cover every value of the closed set it gates on), reading no contract. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/auth/LoginForm.tsx`.

tables: none — no SQL and no db client import in either file; the actions reach GoTrue, not a public table
emits: none — no captureEvent import in src/app/login/page.tsx or src/components/auth/LoginForm.tsx

versioning.why: Its two behaviours are pinned by goldens both directions — the MFA step-up flow and the plain sign-in path each have a rendering test; changing the shape forces a recapture.

inputs.why: Everything it needs arrives through four Server Actions in src/lib/supabase/actions.ts (signIn/signUp/mfaChallenge/mfaVerify) plus the browser client’s signInWithOAuth. contract_ref is empty because none of those five is an /api route and none has a row in the CONTRACT registry — the census counts route files, and this surface reaches none.

outputs.why: It writes only through the Server Actions and waits for the result before advancing — the credentials never produce a client-writable cookie, and the OAuth path only navigates away. contract_ref is empty for the same reason as inputs: a Server Action is not a CONTRACT-registry row.
outputs.rollback: none — a failed action sets an error string and leaves the form exactly as it was; nothing was optimistically applied to roll back.

state.why: Seven useState hooks hold form fields and the MFA challenge, all component-local and all discarded on navigate; no Field Ownership Matrix field is owned, nothing persists, no store.

staleness.why: It displays no server-held value — only what the visitor typed and what the last action returned.

session.why: `/login` is in PUBLIC_PATHS and the lock pins classifyRoute('/login') === 'public'; a signed-in visitor is never bounced away from it.

rls_class.why: The page reaches no table; the Server Actions it calls talk to GoTrue (auth.users), not to a policy-bearing public table.

checks.why: safeRedirectPath is the only thing between the middleware's ?redirect= bounce and an open redirect — it rejects absolute, protocol-relative and backslash forms, and both call sites (dev bypass and onSuccess) must keep going through it.

signInAction only ever reaches aal1; if the mfaRequired branch stops opening the TOTP challenge, an admin silently stays at aal1 and every /api/admin/* call 401s with nothing in the UI saying why — the exact 2026-07-20 defect.

The page reads NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_MODE (client-inlined) while the middleware gate reads the server-only DEV_MODE AND NODE_ENV !== production — the button leaking into a prod bundle must stay harmless, which is a property of the middleware, not of this page.

errors.why:
Every failure sets an error string rendered as a

beside the form — the plain path and the MFA path each have their own.

classes.ui: inline red text under the form, carrying the action's own message
inline red text reading "Authentication failed" / "Verification failed"

no_retry: mfaVerifyAction — a fresh challenge is minted per attempt rather than retrying the old one

emits.why: No captureEvent call and no ledger write anywhere in the page or the form — a sign-in, a sign-up and a failed MFA attempt are all currently uncountable from this surface.

offers.why: No sponsored placement on an auth surface.

metering.why: No usage_events row and no quota — authentication is not a metered product here.

config.why: The one tunable-looking value, the 6-digit code length, is a literal `maxLength={6}` and a `mfaCode.length !== 6` guard, not a registered logic variable.

sharing.why: The four Server Actions are imported by this component and nothing else in src/app or src/components; they have no CONTRACT row, so no other surface can be sharing them.

limitations.what: A backup code cannot be used to complete sign-in.
limitations.measured: Spec 13 §4a makes backup codes a per-request x-admin-backup-code header consumed inside /api/admin/* (verify-admin.ts); there is no GoTrue primitive to mint an aal2 session from one, so the MFA view points the operator elsewhere instead of offering a field.

notes: Empty calls[] is measured, not unlooked: LoginForm reaches the server through Next.js Server Actions (signInAction / signUpAction / mfaChallengeAction / mfaVerifyAction in src/lib/supabase/actions.ts) and the Supabase browser SDK's signInWithOAuth - no /api/* path is fetched anywhere in either file. The 'Continue as Dev' button renders only when NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_MODE=true; the middleware's real bypass reads the server-only DEV_MODE AND NODE_ENV!=='production' (route-guard.ts isDevMode), so the button is cosmetic. Redirect target is guarded by safeRedirectPath (rejects absolute, protocol-relative and backslash forms). MEASURED 2026-09-15: the page holds TWO independently-gated views (credential form and TOTP challenge) but they are one component and one route, so R-13 keeps them one surface rather than promoting the challenge. guards.flag records NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_MODE because it is what THIS page reads (login/page.tsx:7); the security-bearing flag is the server-only DEV_MODE + NODE_ENV pair in route-guard.ts:32-34 — the two are deliberately different vars and the disagreement is the point, not a defect. a11y.touch_target_min_px stays UNRESEARCHED: the submit buttons measure px-4 py-2.5 on text-sm = 40px, which the vocabulary (UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44) cannot express.

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/login') reaches the PUBLIC_PATHS exact-list arm - '/login' is the second entry - and returns 'public'. No earlier arm matches ('/login' is not a PUBLIC_FILE, not under /_next/ or /api/, not '/admin' or '/admin/...', and no PUBLIC_PREFIXES entry is a prefix of it).

programme.why: Used by both products and owned by neither.
